title: Nutritious Chinese Pork Twice Cooked Pork
description: A traditional Chaozhou dish featuring twice-cooked pork, fermented ingredients, and a cheese-pull effect, made with yellow masarepa and low-sodium seasonings. This recipe is a one-pot wonder, perfect for a weeknight dinner.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large pot, combine pork belly, low-sodium soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, ginger, and salt, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 1 hour, or until the pork is tender.
Remove the pork from the pot and let it cool, then slice it into thin strips.
In the same pot, add the fermented bean paste and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add the sliced pork back into the pot and stir to combine with the fermented bean paste.
Sprinkle the yellow masarepa over the top of the pork and stir to combine.
Transfer the pot to the preheated oven and bake for 20 minutes, or until the masarepa is golden brown and the pork is crispy.
Remove the pot from the oven and sprinkle with chopped scallions and black pepper.
Serve the twice-cooked pork hot, garnished with additional scallions if desired.
